MATH 105.description: Antiderivatives, the definite integral, techniques of integration, infinite series, partial derivatives, maxima and minima with constraints, discrete and continuous random variables.

MATH 110.title: Differential Calculus
MATH 110.description: Topics as for MATH 100, but including relevant topics from algebra, geometry, functions, trigonometry, logarithms, and exponentials.

MATH 120.title: Honours Differential Calculus

MATH 200.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

MATH 210.title: Introduction to Mathematical Computing
MATH 210.description: Introduction to mathematical software and numerical methods. Numbers, arrays, functions, vectorization and iteration. Sequences and series, root finding, numerical integration, numerical methods for differential equations, systems of linear equations, mathematical graphics.

MATH 215.title: Elementary Differential Equations I
MATH 215.description: First-order equations; linear equations; linear systems; Laplace transforms; numerical methods; trajectory analysis of plane nonlinear systems. Applications of these topics will be emphasized. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 215.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222
MATH 215.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200

MATH 217.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
MATH 217.description: Partial differentiation, extreme values, multiple integration, vector fields, line and surface integrals, the divergence theorem, Green's and Stokes' theorems. Intended for students in Honours Physics and Engineering Physics. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

a score of 68% or higher in

MATH 220.title: Mathematical Proof
MATH 220.description: Sets and functions; induction; cardinality; properties of the real numbers; sequences, series, and limits. Logic, structure, style, and clarity of proofs emphasized throughout.

MATH 221.title: Matrix Algebra
MATH 221.description: Systems of linear equations, operations on matrices, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization of symmetric matrices. This course is intended for first and second year students. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 221.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 100 or (b) advanced credit for MATH_V 100, or (c) SCIE_V 001 as a corequisite

MATH 223.title: Honours Linear Algebra
MATH 223.description: Matrices, eigenvectors, diagonalization, orthogonality, linear systems, applications. This course is intended for first and second year students. Students who obtain credit for MATH_V 223 cannot in the same or later terms obtain credit for MATH_V 111, MATH_V 152, or MATH_V 221.

MATH 226.title: Advanced Calculus I
MATH 226.description: Functions of several variables: limits, continuity, differentiability; implicit functions; Taylor's theorem; extrema; Lagrange multipliers; multiple integration, Fubini's theorem; improper integrals. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in
a score of 80% or higher in

MATH 226.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 121 or (b) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103
MATH 226.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

MATH 227.title: Advanced Calculus II
MATH 227.description: Parametrization of curves and surfaces; line and surface integrals; theorems of Green, Gauss, Stokes; applications to physics and/or introduction to differential forms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 227.prerequisiteText: MATH 226. Prerequisite grade requirement: 68% in MATH226

MATH 230.title: Marvels of Mathematics
MATH 230.description: A variety of topics in mathematics, showcasing its beauty and utility. Intended for a general audience of students whose degrees have no mathematics requirements, but who may be curious about practical and recreational mathematics. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain UBC credit for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 230.

MATH 253.title: Multivariable Calculus
MATH 253.description: Partial and directional derivatives; maxima and minima; Lagrange multipliers and second derivative test; multiple integrals and applications. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 253.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

MATH 254.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus for Mechanical Engineering
MATH 254.description: Partial differentiation, extreme values, multiple integration, vector fields, line and surface integrals, the divergence and Stokes' theorems; applications to fluid mechanics: buoyancy, hydrostatic force, pipe flow, drag; applications to thermodynamics: work, entropy, heat transfer; numerical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.
MATH 254.prerequisiteText: MATH 101 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

MATH 255.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
MATH 255.description: Review of linear systems; nonlinear equations and applications; phase plane analysis; Laplace transforms; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 255.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223
MATH 255.corequisiteText: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254

MATH 256.title: Differential Equations
MATH 256.description: Linear ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, Fourier series and separation of variables for linear partial differential equations. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 256.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222
MATH 256.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_O 200

MATH 257.title: Partial Differential Equations
MATH 257.description: Introduction to partial differential equations; Fourier series; the heat, wave and potential equations; boundary-value problems; numerical methods. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 257.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258

MATH 258.title: Differential Equations for Mechanical Engineering
MATH 258.description: First-order equations; linear equations; linear systems; Laplace transforms; trajectory analysis of plane nonlinear systems; translational and rotational vibrations; applications to RLC circuit analysis; numerical and graphical methods. Emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.
MATH 258.prerequisiteText: MATH 101 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

MATH 264.title: Vector Calculus for Electrical Engineering
MATH 264.description: Divergence, gradient, curl, theorems of Gauss and Stokes. Applications to Electrostatics and Magnetostatics. MATH_V 264 content is strongly coupled to BMEG_V 220 and ELEC_V 211 with topics and student evaluations weighted accordingly.
MATH 264.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254

MATH 300.title: Introduction to Complex Variables
MATH 300.description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, elementary functions, Cauchy's theorem and contour integration, Laurent series, poles and residues. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 300.corequisiteText: One of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 254, MATH 317

MATH 301.title: Applied Analysis
MATH 301.description: Integrals involving multi-valued functions, conformal mapping and applications, analytic continuation, Laplace and Fourier transforms.
MATH 301.corequisiteText: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312

MATH 302.title: Introduction to Probability
MATH 302.description: Basic notions of probability, random variables, expectation and conditional expectation, limit theorems. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 302.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254

MATH 303.title: Introduction to Stochastic Processes
MATH 303.description: Discrete-time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous time Markov chains, renewal theory. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

MATH 305.title: Applied Complex Analysis
MATH 305.description: Functions of a complex variable, Cauchy-Riemann equations, contour integration, Laurent series, residues, integrals of multi-valued functions, Fourier transforms. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 305.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254
MATH 305.corequisiteText: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312

MATH 307.title: Applied Linear Algebra
MATH 307.description: Applications of linear algebra to problems in science and engineering; use of computer algebra systems for solving problems in linear algebra.
MATH 307.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200

MATH 308.title: Euclidean Geometry
MATH 308.description: Classical plane geometry, solid geometry, spherical trigonometry, polyhedra, linear and affine transformations. Linear algebra proofs are used. It is suggested that MATH 307 be taken concurrently.
MATH 308.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH 152, MATH 221 and one of MATH 220, MATH 226, CPSC 121; or (b) MATH 223

MATH 309.title: Topics in Geometry
MATH 309.description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These may include conic sections, projective configuration, convexity, non-Euclidean geometries, fractal geometry, combinatorial problems of points in the plane.
MATH 309.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) MATH_V 223 or MATH_O 222

MATH 310.title: Abstract Linear Algebra
MATH 310.description: Linear spaces, duality, linear mappings, matrices, determinant and trace, spectral theory, Euclidean structure. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 310.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 152, MATH 221 and one of MATH 220, MATH 226, CPSC 121

MATH 312.title: Introduction to Number Theory
MATH 312.description: Euclidean algorithm, congruences, Fermat's theorem, applications. Some diophantine equations. Distribution of the prime numbers. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 312.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 220, MATH 223, MATH 226, CPSC 121. and 9 additional credits of mathematics courses

MATH 313.title: Topics in Number Theory
MATH 313.description: Topics chosen by the instructor. These might include: division algorithms, group theory, continued fractions, primality testing, factoring. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

MATH 316.title: Elementary Differential Equations II
MATH 316.description: Power series methods (ordinary and regular singular points, Bessel's equation); boundary value problems and separation of variables (Fourier series and other orthogonal series), applications to the vibrating string, heat flow, potentials. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 316.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 215, MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256, MATH_V 258, MATH_O 225

MATH 317.title: Calculus IV
MATH 317.description: Parametrizations, inverse and implicit functions, integrals with respect to length and area; grad, div, and curl, theorems of Green, Gauss, and Stokes. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
notes: One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223 is recommended.

MATH 318.title: Probability with Physical Applications
MATH 318.description: Random variables, discrete and continuous distributions. Random walk, Markov chains, Monte Carlo methods. Characteristic functions, limit laws. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 318.corequisiteText: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312

MATH 319.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
MATH 319.description: Ideas and methods of real analysis and their application. Countability and topology of the reals; convergence, continuity and differentiability of functions; metric spaces. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in
a score of 55% or higher in

MATH 319.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH 220 or (b) a score of 55% or higher in one of MATH 223, MATH 226

MATH 320.title: Real Variables I
MATH 320.description: The real number system; real Euclidean n-space; open, closed, compact, and connected sets; Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem; sequences and series. Continuity and uniform continuity. Differentiability and mean-value theorems. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in
a score of 80% or higher in

MATH 320.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in MATH_V 226 or (b) one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254 and a score of 80% or higher in MATH_V 220

MATH 321.title: Real Variables II
MATH 321.description: The Riemann or Riemann-Stieltjes integrals. Sequences and series of functions, uniform convergence. Approximation of continuous functions by polynomials. Fourier series. Functions from Rm to Rn , inverse and implicit function theorems.

MATH 322.title: Introduction to Group Theory
MATH 322.description: Groups, cosets, homomorphisms, group actions, p-groups, Sylow theorems, composition series, finitely generated Abelian groups. Please consult the Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in
a score of 80% or higher in

MATH 322.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH_V 223, MATH_V 310 or (b) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and a score of 80% or higher in MATH_V 220

MATH 323.title: Introduction to Rings and Modules
MATH 323.description: Rings, ideals, unique factorization, Euclidean rings, fields, polynomial rings, modules; structure theory of modules over a principal ideal domain.

MATH 329.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
MATH 329.description: Ideas and methods of group theory and their applications. Groups, subgroups, and cosets; homomorphisms, isomorphisms, and associated theorems. Consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
MATH 329.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, or (b) MATH_V 223

MATH 335.title: Introduction to Mathematics
MATH 335.description: Intensive course with required tutorial. Combinatorics, probability, geometry and elementary number theory. Not for credit in the Faculty of Science. Students who obtain credit at UBC for any other mathematics course cannot in the same or later years obtain credit for MATH 335. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

MATH 340.title: Introduction to Linear Programming
MATH 340.description: Linear programming problems, dual problems, the simplex algorithm, solution of primal and dual problems, sensitivity analysis. Additional topics chosen from: Karmarkar's algorithm, non-linear programming, game theory, applications.
MATH 340.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

MATH 341.title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
MATH 341.description: Introduction to ideas and methods of discrete mathematics and their application.
MATH 341.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 223, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220, MATH_O 222

MATH 342.title: Algebra and Coding Theory
MATH 342.description: Error-correcting codes via abstract and linear algebra. Emphasis on proofs and computation. Finite fields, Hamming distance and error-correction, upper and lower bounds on the size of a code, linear codes, groups and cosets, encoding and decoding schemes.
MATH 342.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) one of MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

MATH 344.title: Mathematical Game Theory
MATH 344.description: Introduction to mathematical game theory and its applications.
MATH 344.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221 and one of MATH_V 220, MATH_V 226, CPSC_V 121, MATH_O 220; or (b) one of MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

MATH 345.title: Applied Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos
MATH 345.description: Phase plane methods, bifurcation and stability theory, limit-cycle behavior and chaos for nonlinear differential equations with applications to the sciences. Assignments involve the use of computers.

prerequisite.raw: A score of 68% or higher in

MATH 345.prerequisiteText: A score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258

MATH 358.title: Engineering Analysis
MATH 358.description: Fourier series; auto- and cross-correlation; power spectra; discrete Fourier transform; boundary-value problems; numerical methods; partial differential equations; heat, wave, Laplace, Poisson, and wave equations. Applications to mechanical engineering and practical computing applications emphasized.

MATH 360.title: Introduction to Mathematical Modelling
MATH 360.description: Construction and evaluation of deterministic, stochastic, and data-driven models. Software-assisted simulations and numerical solutions involving ordinary differential equations, stochastic processes, and basic machine learning algorithms. Examples from science, engineering, and economics.
MATH 360.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254 and one of MATH 210, CPSC 203, CPSC 210 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258

MATH 361.title: Introduction to Mathematical Biology
MATH 361.description: Mathematical modelling of basic biological processes in ecology, physiology, neuroscience and genetics. Dynamic behavior of difference equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations, explained with reference to concrete biological examples.
MATH 361.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 301, MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258

MATH 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
MATH 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

MATH 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
MATH 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3.5 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

MATH 400.title: Applied Partial Differential Equations
MATH 400.description: Separation of variables, first order equations, Sturm-Liouville theory, integral transform methods.
MATH 400.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 300, MATH 305 and one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312

MATH 401.title: Green's Functions and Variational Methods
MATH 401.description: Green's functions for partial differential equations. Calculus of variations. Eigenfunction expansions. Rayleigh-Ritz and finite element methods. See Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:

children.raw: a score of 80% or higher in

MATH 401.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 80% or higher in one of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312 or (b) MATH 400

MATH 402.title: Calculus of Variations
MATH 402.description: Classical variational problems; necessary conditions of Euler, Weierstrass, Legendre, and Jacobi; Erdmann corner conditions, transversality, convex Lagrangians, fields of extremals, sufficient conditions for optimality, numerical methods; applications to classical mechanics, engineering and economics. Recommended pre-requisites: a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 301, MATH 320, or, a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319.

MATH 403.title: Stabilization and Optimal Control of Dynamical Systems
MATH 403.description: Dynamical systems; stability by Liapunov's direct method; controllability and eigenvalue assignment for autonomous linear systems; linear-quadratic regulator, time optimal control, Pontryagin maximum principle, dynamic programming; applications in engineering, economics and resource management. Recommended pre-requisites: MATH 402, and one of (a) a score of 68% or higher in one of MATH 301, MATH 320, or (b) a score of 80% or higher in MATH 319.

MATH 404.title: Harmonic Analysis I
MATH 404.description: Harmonic analysis on Euclidean spaces, with applications to number theory, partial differential equations and geometric measure theory.

children.raw: a score of 68% or higher in

MATH 404.prerequisiteText: MATH 300 and a score of 68% or higher in MATH 321

MATH 405.title: Numerical Methods for Differential Equations
MATH 405.description: Interpolation, numerical integration, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. Practical computational methods emphasized and basic theory developed through simple models. See Faculty of Science credit exclusion list:
MATH 405.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 256, MATH 257, MATH 316, MATH 358, MECH 358, PHYS 312

MATH 406.title: Variational and Approximate Methods in Applied Mathematics

MATH 418.description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectation, conditional probabilities, convergence of random variables, generating and characteristic functions, weak and strong laws of large numbers, central limit theorem.

MATH 421.title: Real Analysis II
MATH 421.description: Banach spaces, linear operators, bounded and compact operators, strong, weak, and weak* topology. Hahn-Banach, open mapping, and closed graph theorems. Hilbert spaces, symmetric and self-adjoint operators, spectral theory for bounded operators.

MATH 422.title: Fields and Galois Theory
MATH 422.description: Field extensions, the Galois correspondence, finite fields, insolvability in radicals, ruler and compass constructions, additional topics chosen by instructor.

MATH 424.description: The differential geometry of curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space. Mean curvature and Gaussian curvature. Geodesics. Gauss's Theorema Egregium.

MATH 441.description: Formulation of real-world optimization problems using techniques such as linear programming, network flows, integer programming, dynamic programming. Solution by appropriate software.

MATH 442.title: Graphs and Networks
MATH 442.description: Graph theory, emphasizing trees, tree growing algorithms, and proof techniques. Other topics chosen from shortest paths, maximum flows, minimum cost flows, matchings, and graph colouring.

MATH 443.title: Graph Theory
MATH 443.description: Introductory course in mostly non-algorithmic topics including: planarity and Kuratowski's theorem, graph colouring, graph minors, random graphs, cycles in graphs, Ramsey theory, extremal graph theory. Proofs emphasized. Intended for Honours students.

MATH 444.title: Mathematical Research and Writing
MATH 444.description: Current research topics in pure and applied mathematics are explored at the undergraduate level. Technical communication and research skills are developed.

MATH 446.title: Topics in the History of Mathematics I
MATH 446.description: Historical development of concepts and techniques in areas chosen from Geometry, Number Theory, Algebra, Calculus, Probability, Analysis. The focus is on historically significant writings of important contributors and on famous problems of Mathematics.

MATH 448.title: Directed Studies in Mathematics
MATH 448.description: Introduction to the methods of mathematical research through an exploration of a mathematical topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Written report required.

MATH 449.title: Honours Reading
MATH 449.description: Independent reading and research on a mathematical topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Intended for Honours students. Written report required.

MATH 450.title: Asymptotic and Perturbation Methods
MATH 450.description: Asymptotic expansions. Asymptotic evaluation of integrals; WKBJ methods. Regular and singular expansions. Boundary layer theory; matched asymptotic expansions. Multiple scale techniques.

MATH 461.title: Projects in Mathematical Modelling
MATH 461.description: Computational methods for mathematical modelling. Numerical methods for partial differential equations, stochastic processes, and data-driven models. Includes student-directed projects on current research and applications.
MATH 461.prerequisiteText: Either (a) MATH 360 or (b) one of MATH 210, CPSC 203, CPSC 210 and one of MATH 345, MATH 361

MATH 462.title: Projects in Mathematical Biology
MATH 462.description: Development and analysis of mathematical models for complex systems in ecology, evolution, cell biology, neurophysiology, and other biological and medical disciplines.

MATH 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
MATH 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3 1/2 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

MATH 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
MATH 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience involving mathematics in industry for a minimum of 3 1/2 months. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Mathematics Co-operative Education Program.

MATH 515.title: Partial Differential Equations of Fluid Mechanics

MATH 521.title: Numerical Analysis of Partial Differential Equations

MATH 547.title: Optimal Control Theory
MATH 547.description: Optimal control of systems governed by ordinary differential equations. The control problem will be carefully stated, and existence results and necessary conditions will be established. Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman theory will be introduced.

MATH 551.title: Perturbation Methods for Differential Equations
MATH 551.prerequisiteText: MATH_V 550. Ordinary and partial differential equations (MATH_V 400 or equivalent)

MATH 552.title: Introduction to Dynamical Systems
MATH 552.description: Ideas, methods and applications of bifurcation theory and dynamical systems: differential and difference equations, local bifurcations, perturbation methods, chaos. Recommended pre-requisites: one of MATH_V 215, MATH_V 255, MATH_V 256 and one of MATH_V 256, MATH_V 257, MATH_V 316.

MATH 553.title: Advanced Dynamical Systems
MATH 553.description: Topics from: hyperbolic invariant sets and symbolic dynamics, global bifurcations, local bifurcations for partial differential equations, multiple bifurcations, bifurcations and symmetry, applications.

MATH 554.title: Symmetries and Differential Equations
MATH 554.description: Dimensional analysis, modelling, and invariance. Lie groups of transformations, infinitesimal transformations. Applications to ordinary and partial differential equations. No knowledge of group theory will be assumed. Recommended pre-requisite: elementary courses in differential equations and linear algebra.

MATH 557.title: Linear and Nonlinear Waves
MATH 557.description: Classical and recent results in linear and nonlinear waves. Geometrical acoustics and kinematic waves; large amplitude waves in weakly stratified media; small amplitude waves in strongly stratified media. Dispersive waves; group velocity; applications. Recommended pre-requisites: MATH_V 400 and some knowledge of either fluid mechanics or elasticity.

MATH 560.title: Mathematical Biology
MATH 560.description: Mathematical methods in modelling biological processes, at levels from cell biochemistry to community ecology.

MATH 561.title: Mathematics of Infectious Diseases and Immunology
MATH 561.description: Mathematical models for disease spread in populations. Within-host infectious disease dynamics. Models of the immune system and immune cells.

MATH 562.title: Mathematical Electrophysiology
MATH 562.description: Formulation and analysis of models of excitable media. FitzHugh-Nagumo model, ionic models of membrane excitability (e.g., Hodgkin-Huxley), calcium excitability, bursting phenomena.

MATH 563.title: Modelling of Cell-Scale Biology
MATH 563.description: Concepts and techniques for modelling cellular and subcellular dynamics in biological systems. Topics may include complex biochemical systems, biopolymers in cell motility and division, continuum mechanics, and membrane dynamics.

MATH 564.title: Evolutionary Dynamics
MATH 564.description: Mathematical models of evolution and evolutionary game theory. Stochastic dynamics in finite populations, dynamics in spatially structured populations, and adaptive dynamics. Applications include the origin of species and the problem of cooperation.

MATH 590.title: Graduate Seminar
MATH 590.description: Presentation and discussion of recent results in the mathematical literature.
